title: 500. Encode N-ary Tree to Binary Tree

examples.explanation: The N-ary tree encodes to binary as [1,3,null,5,2,null,6,null,4] (first child left, siblings right) and decodes back to the canonical N-ary form.
A single node has no children, so the binary form is just [1].

hints: Parse the N-ary text breadth-first: each null starts the child group of the next queued node.
Encode with the left-child right-sibling rule: first child becomes the left link, later siblings chain through right links.
Decode by walking left once for the first child, then right repeatedly for the remaining siblings.
Emit the binary tree in level order with null placeholders and trailing nulls trimmed, e.g. [1,3,null,5,2,null,6,null,4].
